text: ← RETURN TO SELECTED WORK CASE STUDY 01 · MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM APPLIED AI SYSTEMS MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION LSFM AI HQ — Five AI Agents for My Inbox, Job Search & Code Five Discord agents, each with one job. Each agent calls its own Groq or Gemini model and falls back to the other provider, or uses a local Ollama model on an AMD RX 6600 XT. They sort Gmail into labels and build one-page ATS resumes with headless Edge or Chrome. Job applications wait in an approval channel, and mail is never deleted. PROBLEM Busywork across separate tools: digging through promotional email for the messages that matter, reformatting resumes for each applicant tracking system, switching tabs. CONSTRAINT One person, one PC: five agents in one asyncio event loop, cloud models by default, and no step that deletes mail or sends an application without approval. DECISION One job per agent, each with its own model and a fallback to the other provider. Gmail rules run before the LLM, and heavy jobs (PDF builds, triage) get their own two-thread pool (decisions). MEASURED RESULT LLM round trip 736 ms p50 and 6,177 ms p95 (N=50, 2026-10-02); per agent from 312 ms (Sakura) to 4,861 ms (Yunjin) (telemetry). Email-triage accuracy is not measured yet. LLM ROUND TRIP 736 ms p50 · 6,177 ms p95 N = 50 · 10 per agent · 2026-10-02 Sakura 312 ms Chaewon 786 ms Yunjin 4,861 ms Kazuha 334 ms Eunchae 747 ms 250 ms log scale 8 s Each tick is one recorded run; the tall tick is the p50. Source: 2026-10-02-telemetry.json CODE lsfm-ai-hq (public export of the private build) Explore Agent Architecture ↓ Inference & Hardware Stack ↓ View Code on GitHub ↗ PLATFORM Discord Gateway · Groq + Gemini APIs · Local Workstation DISCIPLINE AI Systems & Agent Architecture ROLE Developer & Systems Builder (Solo) STACK Python 3.11 · Groq + Gemini REST · Ollama (optional) · Headless Edge/Chrome · SQLite ● THE ENGINEERING CHALLENGE Hosted multi-agent setups bill for every model call, so cost grows with each agent and task; they also create brittle single-point-of-failure network dependencies, and hide agent decision states inside terminal black boxes where users cannot intervene. ● THE ARCHITECTURE SOLUTION Engineered an asynchronous 5-agent system on Discord Gateway with operator-selectable routing: per-agent cloud models on Groq and Gemini, each with the other provider as a cross-provider fallback, and a local Ollama mode (qwen2.5-coder:7b on an RX 6600 XT) for private work, switchable live with !mode. Self-Hosted ON A PERSONAL WORKSTATION 3 Modes LOCAL · CLOUD · AUTO ROUTING 5 Agents DISCORD BOTS, ONE EVENT LOOP Single-Page VECTOR ATS PDF OUTPUT 🖥️ Physical Workstation Specs (Local Execution Rig) ● Hosts the 5 Agents PROCESSOR Intel Core i5-12400F 6 Cores · 12 Threads · 4.4 GHz boost GRAPHICS & VRAM AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT 8GB GDDR6 · Optional local inference SYSTEM MEMORY 16GB DDR4 3200MHz Dual-Channel (2 × 8GB) HOSTING Own Workstation No paid servers; cloud calls go to Groq & Gemini APIs ⚡ Resource-Conscious Architecture: In cloud mode, inference runs on Groq and Gemini, so the five agents leave the GPU idle for gaming or rendering. Local mode moves inference onto the RX 6600 XT when keeping prompts on the machine matters more than speed. Show the architecture overview ARCHITECTURE SECTIONS 01. Problem & The Autonomous Vision 02. Design Decisions 03. What Broke & What I’d Change 04. Multi-Agent System Architecture 05. Hybrid Local/Cloud Inference 06. Programmatic Tool Pipelines 07. Guarantees & Failure Modes // 01 · CONTEXT & MOTIVATION Too Many Tabs, Too Much Busywork A lot of my day went to busywork spread across separate tools: digging through promotional email to find the university or banking messages that mattered, reformatting resumes for each applicant tracking system (ATS), and switching between browser tabs. While commercial AI assistants exist, they suffer from two fundamental design flaws: 1. High Recurring Subscription Overhead Cloud-only multi-agent platforms incur unpredictable API token bills and subscription fatigue that scale rapidly without guarantee of uptime or privacy. 2. Monolithic Chatbot Bottleneck A single chat window forced to handle calendar, email, resume formatting, and job tracking collapses under context pollution and loses specialization. “How might we architect a self-hosted operations headquarters where specialized AI agents coordinate autonomously over familiar interfaces, backed by local GPU acceleration?” LSFM AI HQ was engineered from first principles to solve this: a distributed, multi-agent platform running on personal hardware, orchestrating dedicated domain specialists through a unified Discord interface with real-world tool execution. // 02 · DESIGN DECISIONS Design Decisions & Their Costs Each card is one decision: what I chose, what I passed over, why, and what it costs. The evidence links point at the public code or result file at a pinned commit. ADR-LSFM-01 Rules first, the LLM only for unknown mail Decision Sakura's Gmail classifier checks sender, domain and keyword rules first. Only mail no rule recognises goes to the LLM (temperature 0.1). The prompt asks for JSON only; the classifier pulls a JSON object out of the reply when there is one, and falls back to a rule-based label when there isn't. Alternatives Send every email to the LLM. Why Common senders (job platforms, banks, shops, newsletters) get the same label every time with no model call; the LLM only handles the long tail. Cost The rule lists are maintained by hand, and neither tier's accuracy is measured yet: there is no labelled email set. Evidence gmail_engine.py ADR-LSFM-02 A separate two-thread pool for heavy jobs Decision PDF builds (headless Edge, up to 25 s), Gmail triage and sweeps run on their own 2-worker pool. LLM text calls stay on asyncio's default executor. Alternatives Run everything on the default executor. Why A burst of heavy jobs could take every default thread and make quick calls (vitals, chat replies, Obsidian reads) wait behind them. Cost Only two heavy jobs run at once; the rest queue. LLM calls deliberately stay off this pool, or a chat reply would wait behind a PDF build. Evidence heavy_jobs.py // 03 · RETROSPECTIVE What Broke & What I Would Change ⚠️ What Broke in V1 Unbounded asynchronous Discord Gateway event listeners without rate-limit backoff triggered HTTP 429 rate limit exceptions from Groq API during sudden batch notification spikes. ✓ The Engineering Fix Added a second provider: any Groq failure, including a 429, now falls through to Gemini instead of failing the request. What I'd change next: a 429 waits for Groq's Retry-After and a circuit breaker sends a provider that keeps failing to the back of the line, but there's still no jittered backoff after a server error and no shared rate limiter across the five agents, and the HTTP calls are blocking (run in worker threads). V2 moves to an async client with a token bucket and jittered exponential backoff. // 04 · MULTI-AGENT ARCHITECTURE & DELEGATION Five Agents, One Job Each Rather than relying on a monolithic prompt that collapses under context pollution, LSFM AI HQ decomposes operations across five autonomous domain agents. Each agent runs as its own Discord client with its own prompt boundary and tool bindings; run_all.py hosts all five on a single asyncio event loop and pushes blocking tool work (LLM calls, Gmail, PDF builds) onto worker threads: 🌸 Sakura // Chief of Staff & System Orchestrator Operator command ingestion, daily morning briefings, Gmail inbox triage, brain-mode switching, and the inter-agent !apply job-application pipeline. Orchestration · Gmail Triage 🦢 Kazuha // Code & Knowledge Answers questions about the codebase from a SQLite search index and reviews uncommitted changes (!git, !review) before they are committed. Codebase Q&A · Change Reviews 🎨 Yunjin // Document Architect & QA Critic Automated DOM tree auditing, broken-asset scanning across every portfolio page, and LLM-written design critiques with a portfolio health score. DOM Auditing · Design Critique 🐯 Chaewon // Career Strategist & ATS Tailor Job scouting across LinkedIn, Indeed and JobStreet, ATS fit analysis, tailored resume drafting, and headless vector PDF compilation. ATS Vectors · Headless PDF 🥔 Eunchae // System Guardian & Telemetry Hardware vitals watchdog (CPU, RAM and disk via psutil on a 5-minute cycle) with on-demand health reports and check-ins. Hardware Watchdog · Health Reports The 6-Step Request Lifecycle END-TO-END PIPELINE Here is how a real user request travels through the multi-agent system from start to finish: STEP 01 Operator Input Ingest The operator posts a command or a job link in Discord, for example !apply <url>. STEP 02 🌸 Sakura Triage & Context Sakura scrapes the posting, extracts the role and company, and hands each part of the work to the right specialist. STEP 03 Hybrid Router Smart Model Routing Routes to each agent's cloud model on Groq or Gemini (falling back to the other provider on errors), or to the local AMD GPU when the operator selects local mode for private work. STEP 04 Specialist Bot Deterministic Tool Work The assigned bot executes real tools: compiles ATS PDFs, triages Gmail, or checks frontend tokens. STEP 05 🌸 Sakura Assemble the Proposal Combines the tailored resume, curated case studies, and tech pitch into one master proposal. STEP 06 Operator Human Approval The proposal is posted to an approvals channel; nothing is submitted anywhere until the operator reviews it. 🔐 Public code, private data In the public repo: the Obsidian vault client (Local REST API with a filesystem fallback), per-agent model assignments, 429-aware model rotation, the QA audit step in !apply, the scheduled jobs, Ciel's orchestrator and server, and the test suite with CI. Kept private: my vault notes and daily logs, my job-application tracker and resume (the repo ships templates), bot credentials, standalone helper scripts, and the Ciel HUD front end. DATA STAYS PRIVATE // 05 · INFERENCE RUNTIME Multi-Provider Routing: Groq, Gemini & an Optional Local GPU A core engineering priority was high-quality output within provider rate limits without locking the system to one provider. Every agent calls a single dispatcher, query_llm(), whose behavior the operator switches live from Discord with !mode local | cloud | auto: Cloud mode (per-agent model, cross-provider fallback): Each agent has its own cloud model (table below). Sakura, Chaewon, Kazuha and Eunchae go to Groq first; if Groq errors or is rate-limited, the same prompt is retried on Google Gemini (gemini-3.6-flash). Yunjin runs the other way round: Gemini first, then Groq (qwen/qwen3.8-27b) before the call fails. Local mode (Ollama): Runs qwen2.5-coder:7b on the workstation's AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT, keeping prompts on the machine. Local mode fails fast if Ollama isn't running rather than silently sending prompts to the cloud. Auto mode (local first): Probes Ollama with a 1.2 s health check; if it's up, the local model answers, and any local error falls through to the cloud chain above. What it does not do (yet): There is no automatic cloud-to-local failover. When both cloud providers are exhausted in cloud mode, the request fails with the collected provider errors. ENGINE / MODEL ASSIGNED TO PROVIDER WHY WE USE IT qwen/qwen3.8-27b Sakura, Kazuha · default cloud model · Yunjin's fallback Groq Orchestration and code work on Groq's low-latency LPUs. openai/gpt-oss-120b Chaewon Groq The larger model for resume and cover-letter writing. openai/gpt-oss-20b Eunchae Groq A small, fast model for frequent QA and health reports. gemini-3.6-flash Yunjin · cloud fallback for the other four Google Yunjin's design critiques, and a second provider so a Groq outage or rate limit doesn't fail the request. gemini-embedding-001 Kazuha's RAG index Google 3072-dimension embeddings for the SQLite knowledge-base vector store. qwen2.5-coder:7b All agents in local / auto mode Ollama · RX 6600 XT Keeps prompts on the workstation when privacy matters more than output quality. Model names come from DEFAULT_CONFIG in llm_client.py, and the mode and models can be overridden in memory/brain_mode.json. Show the query_llm() code // 06 · REAL-WORLD APIS & TOOLS Deterministic Automation: Headless PDF & Gmail Triage Language models are only as useful as their ability to alter state in the real world. LSFM AI HQ integrates two critical programmatic tools: Headless ATS Resume Compilation Engine Single-Page Strict Formatting via Microsoft Edge PDF_ENGINE Parses structured markdown specifications into calibrated HTML/CSS with exact point-based typography and line heights. Launches Microsoft Edge in headless mode (--headless --disable-gpu --print-to-pdf) to compile a pixel-perfect, 1-page PDF directly to vector format. Renders the resume as real, selectable PDF text rather than an image, so no OCR is needed and it stays parseable by automated Applicant Tracking Systems. Google Workspace OAuth2 Batch Triage Engine Sorts Mail into 10 Labels; Archives, Never Deletes GMAIL_ENGINE Integrates with Google Gmail API using OAuth2 user credential refreshes with secure local token storage. Provisions 10 nested labels (LSFM/Interviews, LSFM/University, LSFM/Finance, LSFM/Clutter) and classifies unread emails using structured JSON prompts. Features an automated !clean sweep that safely archives non-urgent newsletters while keeping critical university, human VIP, and banking notices highlighted. Safety Rules the Agents Can’t Break RELIABLE AUTOMATION · HUMAN IN THE LOOP Autonomous agents are only helpful if you can trust them. LSFM HQ enforces three boundaries: 🛡️ No Delete Path The Gmail engine can only add labels and archive; there is no Gmail trash or delete call anywhere in the codebase. Bulk sweeps (!clean, !cleanse) run only when the operator types the command. 🔒 Credentials Stay Local API keys and OAuth tokens live in git-ignored local files. Cloud mode sends prompts to Groq and Google; switching to local mode keeps inference on the workstation's GPU. 🔄 Independent Reconnects run_all.py starts each bot as its own asyncio task with a reconnect loop and backoff, so one bot's gateway error never takes the other four down. 5 Multi-Surface Interfaces 5 AGENTS · MULTIPLE TOUCHPOINTS LSFM HQ is not locked into a single chat window. Its work shows up across five touchpoints: 💬 Discord Gateway Natural desktop and mobile chat operations with interactive buttons, embeds, and status updates. 🌸 Web Copilot (Sakura) An in-browser BM25 copilot on this portfolio, modeled on Sakura's persona. It runs entirely client-side and is not connected to the live agents. 💻 Setup Scripts Python scripts in scripts/ for Gmail OAuth setup, Discord channel provisioning, and one-time mass inbox sorting. 📥 Gmail Labels Triage results land directly in the inbox as ten LSFM/ labels, visible on any Gmail client. ⚡ Single Launcher python run_all.py starts all five bots in one process, each with its own reconnect loop. // 07 · OPERATING CHARACTERISTICS What the System Guarantees The figures below are properties you can confirm by reading the public code, not performance claims. The one measured number, LLM round-trip latency, is in the footnote with its source; triage accuracy is the next milestone. 0 Servers* Paid Hosting Bots run on a personal workstation 10 Labels Automated Gmail Classification Rules first, LLM for edge cases 0 Deletes Non-Destructive Inbox Sweeps Label + archive only 1 Page ATS Vector Resume Headless Edge, a few seconds per build *No paid servers: the agents run on a personal workstation, and cloud LLM calls go to the Groq and Gemini APIs. API spend isn't stated here because there is no dated billing record to cite yet. LLM round trip (not streamed, as the bots call it): 736 ms p50, 6.18 s p95 over 50 calls, ten per agent, in cloud mode on 2026-10-02, from 312 ms (Sakura, Groq) to 4.86 s (Yunjin, Gemini) at p50 (2026-10-02-telemetry.md). Triage accuracy isn't listed: a labeled email evaluation set is still to be built. Failure Modes & Where the Code Handles Them Each row links to the exact lines in the public repo, pinned to commit 14a319f so the links don't drift, and names the test that exercises it. WHEN THIS FAILS WHAT THE SYSTEM DOES CODE & TEST Discord gateway drops a bot Restarts that bot alone with jittered backoff (3 s, growing 1.5× to 15 s; reset after a session over 60 s). A bad token or missing intents stops it instead of retrying forever. run_all.py L49–83 GatewayRetryTest Groq answers 429 Honours Retry-After (including decimals like 1.5 s) once if it is 4 s or less; otherwise moves to the next Groq model. llm_client.py L212–227 GroqRetryAfterTest Groq answers 413 (request too large) Skips the other Groq models, since each would get the same request, and moves on to Gemini; Groq's reason is logged. The evening rollup caps the day's log it sends at 12 KB, keeping the agents' own posts first. llm_client.py L310–318 sakura_engine.py L228–263 TestRollupDispatchCap The PC restarts mid-morning, or a post is half sent Each scheduled post claims its day before its first message, so it is never sent twice; if writing it fails, nothing is claimed and the next check tries again; if sending fails halfway, one notice names the command to send it by hand (for example !rollup). daily_once.py L41–77 RunDailyTest The bots are started twice The second start exits with the running copy's PID; nothing is killed. instance_lock.py L46–50 InstanceLockTest A whole cloud provider is down Groq agents fall back to Gemini when a Gemini key is configured, and Yunjin (Gemini first) falls back to Groq. If both fail, the error names each provider instead of returning empty text. llm_client.py L376–402 Obsidian's REST API is offline or slow Writes go straight to the vault folder on disk. A lock plus append mode keeps two agents logging at once from overwriting each other. obsidian_client.py L171–205 ObsidianHttpStubTest, DiskAppendTest An LLM-chosen note path tries to leave the vault Rejects ../ and drive paths before anything touches the disk or the REST API. obsidian_client.py L98–111 VaultPathGuardTest A reply is longer than Discord allows Splits it into numbered embeds and clips titles and citation fields to Discord's limits, so a long answer never fails to send. discord_utils.py L122–185 EmbedLimitsTest, ChunkPropertyTest Eunchae's QA review returns no usable score The application package fails QA as "unscored" instead of passing with a default score. eunchae_engine.py L319–337 TestEunchaeQAHonestFailures Email Triage: How Classification Works Sakura's Gmail engine performs automated classification across 10 custom Gmail labels with non-destructive bulk-archiving. Each unread message passes through two tiers: Tier 1 · Deterministic rules: known senders, domains, and keywords map straight to a label with no model call, so common mail is fast and fully predictable. Tier 2 · LLM classifier: anything the rules don't recognize is classified by the LLM into a strict JSON category, parsed defensively, and mapped to one of the LSFM/ labels. Bulk sweeps: !clean and !cleanse archive promotions and newsletters by changing labels only. Nothing is trashed or deleted, so every sweep can be undone from All Mail. 🛠️ Engineering Transparency: How I Built This This system was designed and developed through an iterative AI-assisted engineering workflow. I authored how the 5 agents split the work, designed the structured JSON output contracts, wrote the test suite, and verified every generated prompt and system invariant, while leveraging AI agent pairing (Google Antigravity) for rapid boilerplate scaffolding, API client generation, and documentation review. “The most valuable AI systems are not the largest models, but the ones with the tightest feedback loops, lowest operational friction, and most deterministic tool execution.” ← PREVIOUS CASE STUDY 07 · FinTrack App (FinTech UX) NEXT CASE STUDY → 02 · Manas: Ciel (Voice AI Copilot & HUD)
